jin: Heads-up — spotted intermittent Xid 13 resets on g3-rack4-slot2 during a longscale inference soak yesterday. Node came back up but ECC counts ticked up on GPU1. Attaching quick paste of the dmesg and nvidia-smi snapshot I grabbed.

ada: Can you paste the log inline? we should drain that node before we touch it.

jin: Pasted below. draining now (`kubectl drain node/g3-rack4-slot2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`).

jin: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13, PID=0, GPU=0000:af:00:01
[ 12345.678904] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00:01: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] nvidia 0000:af:00.1: pci bus error: severity=Corrected, type=Data Link Layer, (Transmitted ID), receiver ID 0000:af:00.1
```

jin: ```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0000:af:00.1
  ECC Errors
    Volatile
      Single Bit  : 12
      Double Bit  : 1
```

sam: Ok. plan proposal: do not RMA yet. Run a targeted randomized soak that mixes thermal cycles + high-memory pressure + a small inference-style kernel to try to reproduce and localize. If we can make Xid happen deterministically we can either swap riser/slot or mark card bad.

ada: Agreed. Also capture kernel oops, bus errors, and PCI phys state while running. We should run diag-agent to stream counters to s3 for later correlation: `diag-agent collect --node g3-rack4-slot2 --out s3://redwood-infra/diag/g3-r4-s2/2334509876/`

maya: Capacity note: that node is part of the G3 hitless pool. Draining it will cost us ~0.6 p95 latency during peak if we do long soak during CET hours. Recommend running soak overnight window 0200–0900 UTC and using the spare soak pool nodes. If we need longer we should ask capacity to temporarily bump dedicated pool.

sam: Steps I ran last time — put here so we can copy/paste:
```bash
# baseline: lock node CPU governors, disable power capping changes
ssh root@g3-rack4-slot2 \
  'echo performance > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor'

# run soakbench with randomized thermal and riser toggles
soakbench --gpu 1 --cycles 200 --workload mem_spike,attention_infer --rand-therm 1 --riser-toggle 30s --out ./soak-2334.log
```

jin: What does `--riser-toggle` do?

sam: It toggles power to the PCIe riser via BMC relay every N seconds — simulates intermittent contact. Only run if rack has remote power sequencer; it will cause transient link resets. We use it as a last step — it often reproduces flaky electrical contact.

ada: Let's be careful with riser-toggle on production racks. If someone else shares the PDU we could affect adjacent nodes. Confirm rack-level isolation.

infra-bot: [update] node/g3-rack4-slot2 marked DRAINING by jin at 2334509890

maya: If we can't do riser-toggle, try thermal sweep: `thermal-sweep --gpu 1 --min 30 --max 85 --hold 90s --cycles 300` plus memstress. Thermal variation tends to reveal bad solder joints or cracked BGA.

sam: Also collect periodic snapshots of ECC counters and GPU reset counts:
```bash
while true; do date +%s; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.single_bit,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.double_bit,driver_model.current --format=csv -i 1; sleep 60; done > ecc-timeseries.csv &
```

jin: Good. I'll start a 12h randomized run tonight at 0200 UTC with diag-agent. If it fails early we can escalate.

ada: Return criteria proposal: 24h continuous run with no Xid or GPU reset events and ECC volatile single-bit delta <= 1 over window. If Xid shows again or double-bit increases — escalate to cold-swap + RMA. Document this in the ticket.

maya: For cost tracking — put the soak job on the `infra-soak` billing tag so finance can account for the extra GPU-hours. Use env var `REDFIN_BILLING_TAG=infra-soak-2334509876`.

sam: If the 12h run is clean, run an additional 12h with riser-toggle (if rack safe) or 6h of heavy PCIe stress (pcie_stress --agents 4 --duration 6h). The idea is progressive escalation.

jin: If the 24h passes, can we auto-uncordon and return node? or prefer manual sign-off?

ada: Manual sign-off by infra rotation on-call. We also need perf-sanity: run a 1h inference smoke with Redwood runtime using batch sizes typical for g3 (bs=8, seq=512) to confirm latency & KV cache stability.

sam: Add those commands:
```bash
# inference smoke
rdw-run --model redwood-medium --gpu 1 --batch 8 --seq 512 --duration 1h --trace out/trace.json
```

jin: Noted. I'll kick off tonight and paste links to diag artifacts here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [artifact] diag-agent upload complete -> s3://redwood-infra/diag/g3-r4-s2/2334509876/ (10 files, 45MB)

ada: Ping me after run if you see new Xid or any double-bit ECC increments. If we reproduce, we'll plan a riser swap in morning and re-run.

maya: Scheduling note saved — soak window 0200–0900 UTC tonight. I've reserved the soak pool and added billing tag.

jin: Uploading initial traces now: https://s3.redwood/diag/g3-r4-s2/2334509876/soak-2334.log

sam: Nice. If it reproduces, collect `lspci -vvv` before and after to see if link capabilities or correctable error counts change. Also capture `ethtool -S` if the node is on a host NIC bridge — sometimes NIC interrupts can destabilize power planes.

jin: Will do. Thanks.

ada: One more: add a short checklist to the node ticket so the next on-call has clear steps (drain, baseline snapshot, thermal sweep, memstress, optional riser toggle, RMA threshold). I'll drop a template into the ticket.

maya: :eyes:

jin: Template received. Starting drain -> run at 0200. I'll post results here and close thread when we get 24h clean or decide RMA.

infra-bot: [update] node/g3-rack4-slot2 status DRAINED at 2334509910

sam: Thanks — glhf.
